history.p: The present work, which consists of two sections with text by the Bishop Thomas Kingo, was composed for the church service celebrating the marriage between Prince Vilhelm of Hesse-Cassel and Princess Vilhelmine Caroline of Denmark, King Frederik V’s second oldest daughter. The ceremony took place on 1 September 1764 (see also SchW B2:428) and the chorale was played by an orchestra and vocal ensemble of 54 members. The following week, one of the newspapers recounts the event: 'As soon as the first stanza of the hymn "I Jesu Navn skal al vor Gierning skee", had been sung together with kettledrums and trumpets, the Lord Chamberlain gave signal to Mr. Court Chaplain Qvist to step forward to the bridal stool and perform the wedding ceremony. The text from the Psalms of David (no. 67, stanza 2) had been chosen by Her Royal Highness, the bride herself. When that was finished, and when the last stanza of the mentioned hymn had been sung, the distinguished married couple and all the royal highnesses left in the same order [as they had arrived].' It was a popular piece and was played on several occasions celebrating royal weddings such as two years later, in October, when Princess Sophie Magdalene married Crown Prince Gustav of Sweden, an event described in detail in Wienerisches Diarium; in November 1766 it was performed again, this time celebrating the wedding of Christian VII to Caroline Mathilde in Christiansborg Slotskirke: '[...] As soon as the song, that is the first stanza of the hymn "I Jesu Navn etc.", had been sung together with kettledrums and trumpets, his highness Mr Bishop Harboe stepped forward from the altar [...] When the wedding ceremony finished and the last stanza of the mentioned hymn with instrumental and vocal music had been performed, His Royal Majesty and Her Royal Majesty, the Queen, left.' It was also performed in Aarhus by the cathedral's cantor Henrik Ernst Grosmann, celebrating the marriage between Christian VII and Caroline Mathilde. For this event the instrumentation of the work had been slightly changed omitting brass, timpani and cornettino for instance, presumably reflecting the available instruments in Aarhus.

annot.p: 'Saasnart det første Vers af den Psalme: I JEsu Navn skal al vor Gierning skee, und Pauker og Trompeter var udsiunget, fremtrædde, efter givet Tegn af Ober-Hof-Marechallen, Hr. Hof-Prædikant Qvist til Brude-Skamlen, og forrettede Copulationen, hvortil Texten af Hendes Kongel. Høyhed den høye Brude selv var udvalgt af 67de Davids Psalme 2den Vers. Da samme var til Ende, og med det sidste Vers af bemeldte Psalme besluttet, begave sig det høye Brude-Par og samtlige Kongel. Herskaber i forrige Orden igien tilbage.'
The work was also performed at the wedding for Crown Prince Gustav of Sweden and Princess Sophie Magdalene of Denmark.
Includes an extensive description of the event which took place on the 3 October 1766.

'Saasnart Sangen nemlig det første Vers af den Psalme: I Jesu Navn &c. under Pauker og Trompetter var udsiunget, traadde Hans Høyværdighed Hr. Biskop Harboe frem fra Alteret [...] Da Vielsen var til Ende og det sidste Vers af bemeldte Psalme med Instrumental- og Vocal-Musik var udsiunget, begav Hans Kongelige Majestæt tilligemed Hendes Majestet Dronningen, [...] tilbage.'

physDesc.watermark: the countermark, 'ZOON' and 'HONIG', and the coat-of-arms with a diagonal band and fleur-de-lis is visible (cf. Heawood:64).
physDesc.physMedium: In 2o; upright format originally consisting of limp cover and nested bifolios; title and list of instruments (fol. 1r), blank page (fol. 1v), music (fols. 2r–14v); in all 14 folios numbered 5–30 in ink of which some of the figures are faint due to water stains or trimmed folios. Scheibe's page numbering indicates that the original must have included a limp binding with title page. Hand-ruled paper, a few pages with 20 staves and the remaining have 21 staves (6 mm; single rastrum used) in light brown ink and music in black ink. Source contains numerous changes, cancellations, and additions in ink and should be termed an ink working copy. On the title page V.C. Ravn has added his signature and 'Nr. 5' in ink and 'autograf' has been added in pencil (presumably also Ravn); in the margin of p. 17 a foreign hand – presumably a scribe – has added instrument designations in ink. Bar numbers added in pencil presumably in connection with a modern transcription carried out during the 1940s.

In modern library binding including a soft blue limp binding with flyleaves of which the front flyleaf has a brief introduction explaining the background of the work and that it also once belonged to V.C. Ravn.
